title: Duplicate data at streaming only but not real duplicate exist in the data
question:
I have a delta table and let's call main_table for simplicity. main_table contains N amount of records which have a unique key and it is not duplicate. Let's call unique_id the key.

This delta table is processed by one streaming with the following configuration:

spark.readStream.format("delta").option("readChangeFeed", "true").option("maxFilesPerTrigger", 1000).option("maxBytesPerTrigger", 147483648)\
                          .option("failOnDataLoss", "true")\
                          .load("main_table")\
                          .filter(expr("_change_type not in ('delete', 'update_preimage')"))\
                          .writeStream\
                          .queryName('some_query_name')\
                          .foreachBatch(main_logic)\
                          .option("checkpointLocation", 'some_path_for_checkpoint')\
                          .option("mergeSchema", "true")\
                          .trigger(processingTime='1 seconds')\
                          .start()

The forEachBatch has a function which contains the main logic to process the data, however the logic does a select of the data with a few computations to standardize the data (like convert some metrics into other units) and do a merge, nothing else.

The main function that calls the logic behind its something like this:

def main_logic(df, df_id):
    result = valuesToCompute_Sample.computations(df)
    if not result.isEmpty(): 
        valuesToCompute_Sample.save_merge(result, valuesToCompute_Sample.condition1(valuesToCompute_Sample.partition_table))

The more explicit logict is done using OOP which is the following:

class valuesToCompute_Sample:
    def __init__(self):
        ##### Paths Streaming
        self.singleDeltaTablePath = "somepath"

        self.storageLocation = "destination_path"

    def condition_to_update(self, partition_table):
        cond = f"""(old.partition_table = src.partition_table) AND (old.unique_id  = src.unique_id)"""
        return cond

    def computations(self, main_table): 
        finalvalues = main_table.selectExpr('unique_id','col1', 'col2 * 39.3701 as col2_in_inches',"update_date", "_change_type", "_commit_version", "_commit_timestamp")

        self.finalvalues = finalvalues.withColumn("hash", sha2(concat_ws("", finalvalues)))
        return self.finalvalues

    def save_merge(self, finalDF, condition):
        deltaTable = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, self.storageLocation)
        # Merge two data sets.
        deltaTable.alias("old").merge(finalDF.alias("src"), condition)\
                  .whenMatchedUpdate(condition = "(old.tdpHash != src.tdpHash)")\
                  .whenNotMatchedInsertAll().execute()

For some reason, inside the streaming, the values are duplicated.

Suppose I have the main_table as follows:

| unique_id | col1  | col2 | update_date                   |
|-----------|-------|------|-------------------------------|
| 23411     | 3.5   | 10.1 | 2025-03-11T00:07:05.019+00:00 |
| 23155     | 4.75  | 14.4 | 2025-03-11T00:07:05.062+00:00 |
| 35123     | 123.3 | 9.5  | 2025-03-11T00:07:05.063+00:00 |

unique_id is a long type, col1 & col2 are decimal values and update_date is a timestamp.

If I read the delta table with df = spark.read.format('delta').load("path") and apply a filter to find one unique_id, for example df.where("unique_id = '23155'").display(), I get one result which is correct since it is a unique record.

However, when that is processed in the streaming it duplicates two times the data, but it only happens for a few records:

| unique_id | col1 | col2_in_inches | update_date                   |
|-----------|------|----------------|-------------------------------|
| 23155     | 4.75 | 566.9291       | 2025-03-11T00:07:05.017+00:00 |
| 23155     | 4.75 | 566.9291       | 2025-03-11T00:07:05.067+00:00 |
| 23411     | 3.5  | 397.6378       | 2025-03-11T00:07:05.019+00:00 |
| 35123     | 123.3 | 374.016       | 2025-03-11T00:07:05.063+00:00 |

Key points:

  • Only one record exists: As I explained before, if I do df = spark.read.format('delta').load("path") and then apply the filter to find the record, I get only one record. One problem here, and I'm still looking for information, is that for example the original record has the following value:

    unique_id col1 col2 update_date
    23155 4.75 14.4 2025-03-11T00:07:05.062+00:00

    You can see that the value of update_date is different to the value generated inside the streaming which is the following, but it is the same record:

    unique_id original_value value_1_generated_inside_stream value_2_generated_inside_stream
    23155 2025-03-11T00:07:05.062+00:00 2025-03-11T00:07:05.017+00:00 2025-03-11T00:07:05.067+00:00

    This scenario happens with other records too, but ot looks like there is not a specific pattern or behavior. The unique behavior I have seen so far is that the whole duplicate values satisfy the following:

    • To see the values that are duplicated I call the variable valuesToCompute_Sample.finalvalues and filter for the value. I know they are duplicates since the streaming break with the following error: [DELTA_MULTIPLE_SOURCE_ROW_MATCHING_TARGET_ROW_IN_MERGE] which means the condition for merge consider duplicates values, but as I said it only happens in running the streaming. For example if I execute what it is inside the main_logic not using the readstreaming the merge works ok, since there are not duplicated but If I re run the streaming it breaks.

    • The duplicates values are being checked in the driver node since I do display to see which record got duplicated.

    • The two values that are created inside the stream are one record with a lower timestamp than the original record, and one record has a bigger value than the original record in the delta table. In other words, the value that exists when reading the delta table is always missing and the duplicates values are always a few milliseconds behind and after, but never the one that exist in the original table.

    • Update: Checking the versions of the records I can confirm the following: The streaming generates two diferent versions when reading but not the actual version. For example the current version of the table and the record is 60, but inside the streaming it's reading version 56, 58. This makes more complicated find what it is happening due the fact the table keep getting updates but I will keep investigating.

I suppose there may exist a conflict with the versions that are read in the checkpoints or in the table itself. However, I have no idea how to find what generates this scenario, or what could be the cause for it to happen, since it happens at random times; I mean some records generate this behavior, but most of them does not do that.

I will keep looking for information, and I will review if the record version that exists is the final version that should exist since having one record inside the stream with a bigger timestamp makes me think that the value that it is being kept in the current delta table when reading as a spark.read.format("delta") and not the spark.readStream.format("delta") is not the final version that should exist since it looks like intermediate version due the fact that the update_date is between the two values generated inside the streaming.

I know that I can avoid this problem by applying a window, but I still consider it is not the best solution, or at least it is the last thing I want to apply, and I would like to find the root cause.

That being said:

  • Does anyone have had any similar case like this one?
  • Does anyone have any idea if there are documentation or any type of information that could help me as a guide to start analyzing this behavior?
answer:
I think for delta table we need to give starting version or a starting timestamp so that it does not read all versions every time.

spark.readStream
  .option("startingTimestamp", "2018-10-18")
  .table("user_events")

spark.readStream
  .option("startingVersion", "5")
  .table("user_events")

In addition to that adding skipChangeCommits to true should help fix your issue.
https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/structured-streaming/delta-lake#specify-initial-position
https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/structured-streaming/delta-lake#ignore-updates-and-deletes
